Alright, I also get the honor of presenting our CyberPatriot group. The Osborne CyberPatriot team is an after-school program that teaches students the cyber security skills needed to defend computers and networks. The team meets weekly. Mr. Frederick funds the team registration fee and snacks for the students.

Students learn hands-on system administration skills by configuring Windows and Linux virtual machines to protect against attacks. Students also learn how to configure Cisco switches and routers within a high fidelity network simulation. The CyberPatriot program is a national youth cyber defense competition run by the Air Force Association.

There are over 3,000 teams across the United States teaching students about cybersecurity in a fun and competitive environment. The CyberPatriot team has three competitions held at the high school in October, November and December. The goal of the team is to teach students how to secure computer systems and explore cybersecurity as a career.

The team is led by Mr. Dave Frederick, a retired Lockheed Martin engineer with over 30 years of engineering experience and 16 years of student mentoring. I want to take a moment to publicly thank Mr. Frederick for his unwavering support of not only the CyberPatriot team, but the robotics team as well.
